reference_items.figure_description:
A square grid containing six outlined shapes labeled A through F:
- Shape A: A square measuring 3 units by 3 units.
- Shape B: An irregular stepped polygon with horizontal and vertical edges of varying lengths (not 4 sides, sides of different lengths).
- Shape C: A vertical rectangle measuring 2 units wide and 5 units tall.
- Shape D: A symmetrical 12-sided cross (plus sign) shape composed of five 2-by-2 square sections; every side is 2 units long.
- Shape E: An isosceles trapezoid with a horizontal top base of 4 units, a horizontal bottom base of 6 units, and a height of 4 units.
- Shape F: A square oriented as a rhombus/diamond with horizontal and vertical diagonals measuring 4 units; all 4 sides are of equal length.

reference_items.figure_description:
Six 2D polygon outlines arranged in two rows of three:
- Top row:
  - P: a scalene triangle with a horizontal base.
  - Q: a four-sided quadrilateral resembling a trapezoid, with horizontal top and bottom sides (top shorter than bottom) and slanted right side.
  - R: a diamond/rhombus shape (a square rotated 45 degrees).
- Bottom row:
  - S: a very wide, flat obtuse triangle with a horizontal top-like orientation and a vertex pointing down.
  - T: an isosceles trapezoid with parallel horizontal top and bottom edges (top shorter than bottom).
  - U: a wide obtuse triangle with a horizontal top edge and a vertex pointing downwards.
reference_items.calibration: Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 2003 data, 2007 bridging data, and 2007 data (fourth-grade mathematics).

reference_items.figure_description:
Five identical squares, labeled A through E, each partitioned and shaded differently:
- Option A: The square is divided horizontally into 5 equal strips. The top 2 strips are shaded grey and the bottom 3 strips are unshaded (white).
- Option B: The square is divided by a diagonal from the bottom-left corner to the top-right corner, and a line segment from the center to the bottom-right corner. The entire upper-left triangular half is shaded grey, the right triangular section is shaded grey, and the bottom triangular section is unshaded.
- Option C: The square is divided by two vertical lines into three strips: a narrow shaded strip on the left, a wide unshaded strip in the middle, and a narrow shaded strip on the right.
- Option D: An unshaded triangle has its base along the entire bottom edge of the square and its apex at the midpoint of the top edge. The two right triangles flanking it on the left and right are shaded grey.
- Option E: The square is divided by two vertical lines into 3 equal-width vertical strips. The left strip and the right strip are shaded grey, and the middle strip is unshaded.
reference_items.calibration: Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 1995 and 2003 fourth-grade mathematics data.

slope.instructions: TIMSS scaled this 1-point item with the two-parameter logistic (2PL) model, which TIMSS uses for constructed-response items worth 1 point, in the calibration "Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 2003 data, 2007 bridging data, and 2007 data (fourth-grade mathematics)". What is the item's slope (discrimination) parameter a? A higher a means that the item separates students of lower and higher mathematics ability more sharply. Choose the value closest to it. The state also lists reference items: the calibrated TIMSS items of the same grade most similar to this one (never the item itself or its other parts), most similar first, with their percent correct and their calibrated parameters, each on the scale of its own calibration. Use them to place this item.

location.instructions: TIMSS scaled this 1-point item with the two-parameter logistic (2PL) model, which TIMSS uses for constructed-response items worth 1 point, in the calibration "Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 2003 data, 2007 bridging data, and 2007 data (fourth-grade mathematics)". What is the item's location (difficulty) parameter b? b is on a logit scale on which the students of the calibration average about 0; a higher b means a harder item. Choose the value closest to it. The state also lists reference items: the calibrated TIMSS items of the same grade most similar to this one (never the item itself or its other parts), most similar first, with their percent correct and their calibrated parameters, each on the scale of its own calibration.
